title: EngramPort capability reference and grant v1, revision 2
description: Normative. A descriptor says a capability exists; a grant says a principal may use it. Neither carries a credential and neither is invocable. Revision 2 replaces revision 1's permissive provider payload after adversarial review demonstrated three bypasses: nested secrets inside a free-form input_shape, a bearer value in provider_installation_ref, and a kind/payload mismatch. See docs/security/setup-credential-threat-model.md sections 4 and 5.
$comment: SCHEMA LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. JSON Schema constrains structure. It cannot recursively detect secret-shaped CONTENT, and this schema no longer pretends to. Structural closure here is paired with a mandatory ingest validator specified in $defs.ingest_requirements. A record passing this schema is well-formed, not trusted.

ingest_requirements.$comment: NORMATIVE PROSE, not validated by this document. An ingest validator MUST implement all of these before any descriptor is stored or rendered. Threat model control A5 gates them.
requirements: Recursively scan every string in the record, at any depth, with the credential detector of finding F10. Reject the whole record on any hit; do not strip and continue.
Reject any string that parses as a URL carrying authority: userinfo, a query or fragment parameter named like a token, or a scheme outside https.
Reject any string matching a bearer-token shape, including 'Bearer ' prefixes, JWT triples, and PEM blocks.
Enforce a total record byte ceiling and a maximum nesting depth, so scanning cannot be exhausted.
Resolve shape_ref against a locally registered shape registry. Never accept an inline provider-supplied schema.
Fail closed: a detector or resolver error rejects the record.

safe_text.$comment: Provider-supplied display text. Bounded, and still subject to recursive content scanning at ingest.

identifier.$comment: Deliberately narrow. Excludes whitespace, quotes, slashes and control characters, so an identifier cannot smuggle a URL, a PEM block, or a bearer header.

secret_ref.$comment: How a credential is pointed at, never carried. Custody model B or C in threat model section 5.

manager.$comment: Revision 1 allowed a local env-file manager, which contradicted the claim that only an authorized server-side consumer can resolve a reference. Removed.

locator.$comment: Deliberately TIGHTER than $defs/identifier, which permits dots for capability names like github.read_contents. A JWT is dot-separated base64url and therefore matched the identifier grammar; agent-a's own probe of revision 2 caught a JWT passing as a locator. Dots are excluded here. A PEM block fails on its leading dash, a connection string on its slashes and at-sign, a JWT on its dots.

descriptor.$comment: What a connector advertises. Attacker-influenced input from threat actor A6. Closed: no additional properties, no free-form object anywhere, and NO field from which an invocation locator may be read.

shape_ref.$comment: Replaces revision 1's input_shape, which was a free-form object and accepted {token, nested:{private_key}}. A descriptor now REFERENCES a locally registered shape by identifier; it never carries one. The registry is local, so a provider cannot define the shape it is validated against.

trust.$comment: A descriptor is never more trusted than this. It came from outside.

invocable.$comment: Required and constant. A descriptor asserts its own non-invocability, so any code path treating one as invocable contradicts a field it must have read. provider_installation_ref is REMOVED: revision 1 allowed 'Bearer REAL_SECRET' there, and an implementer could hand that opaque value to a provider SDK. Installation locators now come only from the grant store.

grant.$comment: The authorization decision. Resolved server-side at call time; possession of this record is not authority.

granted_by_principal_id.$comment: A grant never exceeds the granting principal's own authority, resolved per threat model section 6, never asserted by the caller.

installation_locator.$comment: Lives on the GRANT, never on the descriptor. This is the field an invocation may read, and it exists only because an authorized grant put it here.

expires_at.$comment: Absolute and required. Unbounded grants are not expressible. Enforced by the datastore per constraint C6, not only by application sweeps.

$comment2: kind is now COUPLED to the payload branch. Revision 1 used a bare oneOf on required-payload, which accepted kind:capability_grant carrying only a descriptor. Each branch below pins the kind, requires its own payload, and forbids the other.
